Earlier today radio stations in North Western View, as well as ships in the Nestor ocean, picked up a mysterious message from a ship, the message was an SOS, but it also had a lot of static as well as what sounded like a fire alarm, and rushing water. Rescue teams were sent to the area, but they only found a single sheet of paper, with the faded words Leviathan. Operators soon realized that the SS Leviathan was the only ship unaccounted for. The SS Leviathan was a Leviathan class oil tanker, carrying 2 million tons of oil, headed for Eastornia-Kolionia. Many speculate that the ship was attacked, seeing that it's route led it close to a country in active war, though many say it is unlikely for SS Leviathan to be attacked, after all it was flying the Western View flag, and wasn't in an active war zone, and the Leviathan's coordinates suggest it was hit by a large storm, but since there have been no survivors found yet, we can only go by the single radio message the Leviathan sent.

Other facts about the SS Leviathan.
[list][*]The SS Leviathan is the largest Wessern ship ever built, at almost 1,000ft long.
[*]The SS Leviathan could carry up to 3 million tons of oil.
[*]The SS Leviathan entered service around 2 years ago, and it builders 4 years to build
[*]The SS Leviathan housed 40 crew memebers
[*]The SS Leviathan could go 17 knots in clear weather
[*]The SS Leviathan was considered to most advanced Wessern ship
[*]The SS Leviathan was built and launched in Wessernia, Western View's capital[/spoiler]

Trying again because I forgot to do some things
Expansion of Kaaganikan Territory
July 14th, 2025
1359 words, 6795 pixels
https://imgur.com/a/yhWVGVM
GDP change: 92 million marks > 112 million marks
GDP per capita change: 6571 marks > 6666 marks
Population change: 14.3 million > 16.8 million
Note: I have no idea how to count pixels. Please tell me if Im asking for too much.
Also please tell me if Im not actually touching the iron deposits that I expanded towards.

[spoiler=RP]
Kaaganikan forces are storming across the desert sands, driving through territory that has mostly gone without meddling by civilization. The government has sent them on an order to plant a flag at a faraway location and bring high power explosives and drills. There was little explanation on the matter other than to start drilling once the forces make it to said point.

The captain of the operation, Lieutenant Jelloun, was in one of the vehicles, and was in charge of planting a flag on just about every point of interest they saw coming. There was the occasional settlement built on a water source, and for the most part, they were willing to offer water and supplies out of goodwill and intimidation. One of the soldiers in the Lieutenants vehicle asks about the drills.

They wanted us to crack into something once we got there. Apparently theyve been eyeing this spot up for a while, but they are a bit prudish when it comes to explanation.

Well youd think we wouldnt need to dig up anything, we sit on an ocean of copper. We have metals to sell, what could possibly be out here? he says, with a hint of arrogance. This was not a fun task for anybody involved.

The aged Lieutenant thinks for a moment, with a calm but thoughtful expression on his face.
Politics. Its politics. Its always been for politics.
Its because those sitting on their desks in those skyscrapers have never had to drive for hours through desert so they can drill for whoever knows what.
The old man continues muttering about something, but the soldier simply looks out the window, halfway listening. It was about 20 minutes later that they finally reached their destination. The men leave their vehicles and take in the sight. A lot of them are just now realizing the difference between here and Kaaganika. It was moderately more temperate than the homeland and the geography was mildly more green and lush. The Lieutenant calls the military head of operations on his phone.
Sir, I made it to the desired location. What do you need us looking for? Over.
I need you to have your men drill the rock and look for gray, shiny dust. Any of it. I dont want to see any stone unturned in these parts.

It then clicked. Kaaganika needed her own iron. He had to give the orders now.
He called on a megaphone to his men, of which there were around two or three dozen of them.
I need you gentlemen to use your drills and look for shiny, gray rocks. Any amount is fine, doesnt matter if its powder or dust, we just need something.

The men responded with a yes sir and began digging. Lieutenant Jelloun was thinking of what this implies. If Kaaganika was trying to claim land and iron, then what is it preparing for? What is going to happen? He had already fought for the Workers Republic in the brief civil war that recently took place, and the memories of modern day trench warfare were fresh on his mind. That was warfare for impoverished nations. Nations without modern bombers or missile launchers. If Kaaganika claimed this land and the iron for itself, then it could surely go toe to toe with at least Baladullah.
He doubted an invasion of the nation was a smart move. Kaaganikas external situation is shoddy at best, and invading a neighbor with a lack of a good reason is a terrible idea, especially considering they also sit on a sea of copper.
But what about Sikirsk?
Sikirsk would trample Kaaganika to the ground, no doubt, but maybe with the Kaiserreichs help, it could open a painful new front for the Sikirskans. However the IPEA stood right on her doorstep, and any intervention could end up with a Baladullan invasion or international sanctions.

The Lieutenant had made up his mind, a thought definitely in Kaaganikas leadership.
Kaaganika stood at an unbelievably awkward position in world affairs. They needed to prepare for the joining of any potential conflict against anybody. They could no longer rely on those across the world.
He did not notice a small soldier standing next to him, holding a small, silver-colored rock. He had been drifting off for about 30 minutes.
Sir, I have found a silver rock, sir.
He inspected the rock, and tested its magnetic properties.
When the rock drifted to the magnet, he confirmed that it was indeed iron. He told his men to gather whatever rocks they had and test for iron, some were positive, some were negative. He called the head of operations about the success.
Now you need to plant a flag down, and call Tazi. She is awaiting your call as we speak.
This old man was given a large task, far above the duties of his rank. Nevertheless, a call was made to Tazi. She didnt answer the first time. He took a risky move and called her again, to which she picked up.
Maam, I come with good news. There is iron here.
Oh really? Thats good news! Hold on, call you in a bit, I gotta tell my, what was it, parliament, about the news! Ok byeee!
Wait, what!?
The phone call ended before he could say anything else. The old man was in shock. He had forgotten that a 24 year old Llyndoran had taken power of Kaaganika after Ayoubs unfortunate death.

Monika Tazi, however, was not shocked. A few hours later, she walked up to a podium, in front of the Kaaganikan leadership, with a map in hand and a grin stretching from ear to ear, wearing a crop-top with the newly designed Kaaganikan sun on it, used as the rulings partys main symbol. Definitely not matching the parliamentary style of gray suits and polished black shoes. She walked up to the podium and began her first ever speech shown to the public.

Hi everybody! I bring yall here to announce that I made a brand new province of Kaaganika., she begins. Despite only being in West Shamat for a few years, she spoke the language alright. Im going to name this province Al-Ayoub, in honor of you know who.
She then pulls up her map of Kaaganika, and in an almost hilarious fashion, she had quite literally drawn a straight line as the new northern border. Some were shocked, some were happy, some were surprised, but many were proud, as this girl did just expand their nations territory.

She goes on with her speech, explaining the inner workings of the new state and some of her future plans. The point was made however: Monika Tazi ruling over Kaaganika was not a fib, or a pun, or a joke. She planned to ride the political train, wherever it might take her.

To say that the public of both Kaaganika and those who cared around the world were surprised is an understatement. Those under the Islamic religion, particularly the more radical ones among them, took this with suspicion. However, others in Kaaganika took it with open arms, arguing that there should be no fighting over Anikan or Kaagan if the leader isnt of either ethnicity. But the point was made clear. She was not planning to hand over here position to some aged politician. She was here to stay

She finishes her speech about 15 minutes later, and is met with applause by the crowd. The public is left to their own devices on how they feel about it and how they handle it. One thing Monika did mention was the iron reserves in the new territory. This made most people excited, as it meant that iron mines and refineries were probably going to be constructed, as well as the building of a road to connect iron mines to the heartland. The leadership were also particularly pleased, as they saw that a majority of people were glad for the new expansion, as well as some peoples willingness to work with Monika instead of trying to overthrow her. Mostly. She had a lot to do before she could sit back in her chair.[/spoiler]
